name: Shia Islamism
summary: Shia Islamism is the implementation of Twelver Shia Islam in politics, wanting public life and law organised around an Islamic vision. It includes Khomeinism, which gives supreme authority to a qualified jurist, and Iraqi movements such as the Dawa Party, which taught rule of the people and, in part, rejects clerical rule. The branches share the aim of an Islamic order but split on clerical rule, democracy and relations with Iran.
scope: The family of Shia Islamist political traditions (Khomeinism, Dawa and Sadr's school, related movements), not Shia Islam as a religion, Shia voters generally, or Khomeinism alone. Answers rest on positions that the scholarship and the programmes of both the Iranian and Iraqi branches share; positions held by one branch only are null, and documented disagreements are split answers. Quietist clergy such as Sistani are cited only as one side of a split.
